title: Veer Pahariya Announces Prem Keetanu for Gandhi Jayanti Release
excerpt: The Hindi entertainer, widely reported as the official remake of Malayalam blockbuster Premalu, stars Pahariya alongside Aparshakti Khurana and debutant Aafiya Sayed, arriving in cinemas on October 2, 2026.
body:
• Veer Pahariya's second film Prem Keetanu is set for a worldwide theatrical release on October 2, 2026, coinciding with Gandhi Jayanti.
  • The film is widely reported as the official Hindi remake of the 2024 Malayalam blockbuster Premalu, which earned over ₹109 crore worldwide.
  • Directed by Apoorv Singh Karki (Sirf Ek Bandaa Kaafi Hai, Aspirants), the cast includes Aparshakti Khurana, debutant Aafiya Sayed, Rakesh Bedi, and Nikhil Vijay.
  • The project marks the debut production of Gaurav Verma's Avanika Films banner, co-presented by Phars Films.

Veer Pahariya has announced his second film. Prem Keetanu, a youth-driven entertainer about college life, friendships, and heartbreak, will release in cinemas worldwide on October 2, 2026. The announcement, made via social media with the film's first poster, positions the project as a sharp tonal shift from Pahariya's debut in Sky Force, the Akshay Kumar-led aerial action drama.

The Premalu Connection

Earlier reports from multiple trade outlets identified Prem Keetanu as the official Hindi remake of Premalu, the 2024 Malayalam romantic comedy directed by Girish A D that became a surprise box office phenomenon. The original earned over ₹109 crore worldwide, driven by strong word-of-mouth and a repeat-viewing audience that kept the film in theatres for weeks. Its Hindi-dubbed OTT release further expanded its reach, creating clear demand for a full-fledged Hindi adaptation.

While the official announcement of Prem Keetanu does not explicitly reference Premalu, the casting of Aafiya Sayed — identified in earlier trade reports as the female lead in the Premalu remake — and producer Gaurav Verma's involvement align with the previously reported development. Verma, who headed Red Chillies Entertainment and co-produced Shah Rukh Khan's Jawan, brings mainstream sensibility to the project.

Cast and Creative Team

The ensemble includes Aparshakti Khurana, a consistent performer in the comedy-drama space, alongside Rakesh Bedi and Nikhil Vijay. The film is directed by Apoorv Singh Karki, whose credits include the courtroom drama Sirf Ek Bandaa Kaafi Hai and the widely acclaimed web series Aspirants.

Sharing the first poster, Pahariya wrote: "Na marks mile, na job, na hi pyaar… bas toote hue dil aur acche dost leke aa rahe hain #PremKeetanu." The tagline signals a relatable, slice-of-life tone targeting younger audiences.

"Na marks mile, na job, na hi pyaar… bas toote hue dil aur acche dost leke aa rahe hain."

— Veer Pahariya, announcing Prem Keetanu

Pahariya's Career Trajectory

For Pahariya, who comes from a prominent political family and studied theatre in the United States, Prem Keetanu represents a deliberate effort to diversify early. His debut in Sky Force was watched closely — he played Indian Air Force officer T. Vijaya alongside Akshay Kumar. Moving from a patriotic action film to a breezy college romance demonstrates range-building that Bollywood newcomers rarely attempt in their second project.

He also has Naam – To Live Is War, a dark action thriller presented by Mahesh Bhatt, in his upcoming lineup.

What's Next

The Gandhi Jayanti release date places Prem Keetanu in a competitive holiday window. For diaspora audiences, the film carries added curiosity — Premalu was a genuine crossover hit that found audiences well beyond Kerala, and its Hindi adaptation will test whether the original's charm can translate across languages with a new cast.
